properties.name: Lake Chad
properties.summary: Shallow endorheic lake shared with Chad, Niger, and Cameroon; open water has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s.
properties.description: Lake Chad once covered more than 25,000 km². Open water is now a fraction of that, replaced by marshes and receding shorelines. Nigeria's shoreline lies mainly in Borno and Yobe. The lake still supports fishing, recession agriculture, and transhumant pastoralism, and remains a focus of the Lake Chad Basin Commission.
properties.areaNote: ~1,350 km² open water (highly variable; far below 1960s extent)
properties.usage: Fishing, pastoralism, flood-recession farming, cross-border trade.
properties.ecology: Wetland birds, seasonal inundation, desertification pressure, invasive typha in some channels.
properties.climate: Sahel; rainfall decline and irrigation upstream affect inflows (Chari–Logone dominate).
properties.significance: UNESCO concern over shrinkage; security and livelihood hotspot of the basin.
properties.highlights: ["Shared by four countries","Severe 20th-century shrinkage","Livelihoods for millions in the basin"]

properties.name: Kainji Lake
properties.summary: Nigeria's largest man-made lake, impounded by Kainji Dam (1968).
properties.description: Kainji Dam was a flagship independent-era hydropower project. The lake drowned settlements and created a major fishery and Kainji Lake National Park on adjoining shores. Water level and generation vary with Niger River flow and plant maintenance cycles.
properties.maxDepthNote: ~12 m average; deeper near dam wall
properties.usage: Hydroelectric power, fishing, limited navigation, tourism (national park).
properties.ecology: Reservoir fishery; drawdown agriculture; wildlife in Kainji Lake National Park.
properties.significance: First large Nigerian hydro dam; anchor of Niger State's Power State identity.
properties.highlights: ["1968 Kainji Dam","Largest reservoir in Nigeria","National park shoreline"]

properties.name: Lagos Lagoon
properties.summary: Barrier-island lagoon behind Lagos; linked to the Atlantic through creeks and the harbour.
properties.description: The lagoon is the water body that made Lagos a port city. It receives Ogun and Osun drainage, urban wastewater, and sand-mining pressure. Water transport (Lagos Waterways) and fishing remain active despite pollution and siltation.
properties.maxDepthNote: ~2–5 m in main channels; shallower in flats
properties.usage: Fishing, sand mining, urban drainage, ferry transport, port access.
properties.ecology: Brackish water, mangroves (degraded), urban pollution hotspots.
properties.significance: Historic harbour of Eko; Lekki–Lagos urban waterfront.
properties.highlights: ["Made Lagos a port","Ferry network","Urban environmental pressure"]

properties.name: Oguta Lake
properties.summary: Imo State's largest natural lake; a tourism and fishing landmark in the southeast.
properties.description: Oguta Lake is a palm-fringed natural lake fed by the Njaba and Utu rivers. It hosts the Oguta Lake Holiday Complex, boat regattas, and lakeside settlements. Oil-palm processing and fishing sustain local communities.
properties.usage: Tourism, fishing, boat transport, cultural festivals.
properties.ecology: Freshwater fish species, riparian vegetation, linked wetland channels.
properties.significance: Major natural lake of the Niger Delta hinterland; Imo tourism icon.
properties.highlights: ["Oguta Lake Holiday Complex","Annual regatta","Two-river inflow (Njaba / Utu)"]

properties.name: Goronyo Reservoir
properties.summary: Large Sokoto basin reservoir supplying irrigation and downstream communities.
properties.description: Goronyo Dam impounds the Rima River to provide dry-season irrigation for the Sokoto–Rima basin and water for Sokoto city. Siltation and variable rainfall affect storage capacity.
properties.ecology: Seasonal drawdown exposes mudflats; bird habitat in wet season.
properties.significance: Key water-security asset for northwest Nigeria.

properties.name: Dadin Kowa Reservoir
properties.summary: Gombe State reservoir on the Gongola, supporting hydropower and irrigation.
properties.description: Dadin Kowa Dam regulates the Gongola River for the Dadin Kowa hydro plant and downstream irrigation in the Upper Benue basin. The reservoir also supports fishing and livestock watering.
properties.significance: Major Gongola basin water infrastructure in the northeast.
properties.highlights: ["Gongola River regulation","Linked hydro plant","Upper Benue irrigation"]

properties.name: Asejire Reservoir
properties.summary: Oyo State reservoir on the Oshun River, supplying Ibadan and surrounding farms.
properties.description: Asejire Dam was built in the late 1960s to provide water for Ibadan and irrigation in the Oshun valley. The lake is a weekend recreation spot and supports a local fishery.
properties.usage: Domestic water for Ibadan, irrigation, fishing, recreation.
properties.significance: Primary water source for Nigeria's third-largest city.

properties.name: Challawa Gorge Reservoir
properties.summary: Kano basin reservoir feeding irrigation and the Challawa hydro plant.
properties.description: Challawa Gorge Dam impounds the Challawa River tributary of the Hadejia–Jama'are system. It supports Kano's hinterland irrigation schemes and the Challawa Gorge hydroelectric station.
properties.significance: Part of the Hadejia–Jama'are basin water infrastructure.
properties.highlights: ["Kano irrigation supply","Linked hydro plant","Hadejia system tributary"]
